title: Harden MediaPipeline launch section: mode gating, slice fatal exits, loader contract
summary: Fixes seven launch-section code-review findings in ops/pipeline/entrypoints/MediaPipeline.ps1 and its startup slices: (1) worker children and the lockless -DumpEffectiveConfigPath mode no longer delete the shared pause/stop flags; (2) -DumpEffectiveConfigPath no longer sweeps temp/stale-partial files, repairs worker claims, blanks the active-jobs file, or writes the progress file (it is now actually read-only as documented); (3) -ValidateOnly no longer writes the shared progress file; (4) the module loader load-order/manifest dual source of truth is enforced by a startup contract check and the silent legacy Modules fallback is removed; (5) post-lock fatal exits now run ExitCleanup explicitly; (6) the config import uses -LiteralPath; (7) dead code removed ($args relaunch branch, $requiredKeys/$arrayKeys, $moduleRoot). Additionally fixes a latent slice-extraction regression discovered during validation: exit inside a dot-sourced slice does not terminate the entrypoint in PowerShell 7, so the FATAL paths in module_loader.ps1 (missing module), runtime_paths.ps1 (worker-arg validation, exit 74), and startup_path_validation.ps1 (unreachable LocalBase, exit 2) printed FATAL but let the pipeline keep running; slices now set $startupFatalExitCode and the entrypoint exits on their behalf after each dot-source.
reason: Operator-approved remediation of a launch-section code review (chat, 2026-06-10). The flag-deletion race could silently cancel an operator pause/stop request whenever a parallel-encode worker child started; the lockless dump/validate modes could mutate live pipeline state from a mode documented as read-only; and the dot-sourced exit semantics meant startup FATALs (including an unreachable LocalBase) did not actually stop the pipeline.
behavior_before: Every non-ValidateOnly invocation (including -WorkerChild and -DumpEffectiveConfigPath) deleted the shared pause/stop flags and ran Clear-OldTempFiles/Clear-StalePartialFiles; dump mode also repaired worker claims, overwrote the active-jobs file with an empty list plus a compatibility progress write, and wrote progress stage idle, all without holding the instance lock; -ValidateOnly wrote progress stages startup then idle. A drifted module-loader name silently fell back to the nonexistent legacy entrypoints/Modules path. exit 74/2/1 inside the dot-sourced startup slices aborted only the slice file and the entrypoint continued running.
behavior_after: Pause/stop flag cleanup and temp/stale-partial sweeps run only for controller-style runs (not WorkerChild, not DumpEffectiveConfigPath); claims repair and the active-jobs reset additionally skip dump mode; dump and ValidateOnly write no progress stages. The loader validates load order and manifest describe the same module set and fails fast on drift. Slice FATALs set $startupFatalExitCode and the entrypoint exits with the intended code (74 worker args, 2 LocalBase, 1 loader) immediately after the slice returns, running ExitCleanup where the lock is already held.

operator_validation_required: AGENTS.md section 7 (queue launch scope / settings paths are touched): a real -Once or continuous run, including at least one parallel-encode worker-child dispatch, confirming pause/stop flags set mid-run are honored and worker results are consumed normally.
